seo.metaDescription: Style tally-charts with the --ch-* tokens, the data-ch-part attribute and the data-ch-* state attributes; force a theme on any element.

props.markdown: Every color, size and motion setting of a chart is a CSS custom property called `--ch-<name>`, a token. Import `tally-charts/theme.css` once and the tokens are defined for the light and the dark theme; change one on any element and every chart below it follows. This page lists the tokens, shows how to aim at a single part of a chart, and explains how to force a theme on part of the page.

The theme tokens change between the light and the dark theme. The values are read from `theme.css`, so the table is always the shipped one. Default values can be tuned in a minor release, for example to keep a contrast ratio; the names and their meaning are stable.
The shared tokens have one value for both themes: sizes, hatching, motion and the sequential ramp.

props.text: Tokens without a default in theme.css

props.markdown:
These tokens are public too, but `theme.css` does not declare them for every chart, so they are not in the tables above. Set them on any element to change the charts below it.

- `--ch-zone-marker`: the color of the `ZoneMeter` marker.
- `--ch-seq-base`: the base color of the sequential ramp. It defaults to `--ch-loss`.
- `--ch-seq-mix-1`, `--ch-seq-mix-2`, `--ch-seq-mix-3`, `--ch-seq-mix-4` and `--ch-seq-mix-5`: the share of the base color in each level.
- `--ch-seq-1`, `--ch-seq-2`, `--ch-seq-3`, `--ch-seq-4` and `--ch-seq-5`: the five levels, computed from the base and the mixes on every chart, legend and heatmap. Read them, but steer them with the base and the mixes, because overriding them has no effect.
- `--ch-heatmap-cell-height`: the height of a `Heatmap` cell. Default `44px`.
- `--ch-heatmap-min-cell`: the narrowest a `Heatmap` column gets before the grid scrolls sideways. Default `56px`.

`data-ch-seq-tone="<tone>"` on an ancestor picks that tone's base and its shares for the current theme. `Heatmap`'s `tone` prop sets it for you. The attribute must sit on, or below, the element that sets `data-ch-theme`, or the ramp is computed in the outer theme.

Tokens are inherited, so a `style` on a container (or a rule in your own stylesheet) reaches every chart inside it. A token can be set to a color, a number or another token: below, `--ch-accent` is pointed at `--ch-loss`, and `--ch-radius` and `--ch-hatch-gap` are plain numbers. The chart on the left is untouched.

Colors that follow the theme belong in a token or in `var(--ch-*)`, not in a fixed hex value, or the chart will look wrong in the other theme. The `--ch-seq-1` to `--ch-seq-5` tokens are computed from `--ch-seq-base` and the `--ch-seq-mix-*` tokens, so steer those instead of overriding the computed ones.

To change something a token does not cover, select the part with `[data-ch-part="…"]`, for example `tooltip` or `callout-stem`. The part names are stable. The classes `ch-*` and the `--_ch-*` variables are private and can change in any release, so never select those.

The state and variant attributes are stable too, names and values:

- `data-ch-tone`: the tone of a mark or a piece (`accent`, `accent-soft`, `loss`, `warn`, `gain` or `neutral`).
- `data-ch-fill`: how a mark is filled (`solid`, `hatch` or `hatch-fade`).
- `data-ch-active`: set on the mark the pointer or the keyboard is on.
- `data-ch-dimmed`: set on the marks that are not the active one.
- `data-ch-direction`: the way a bar grows (`up`, `down`, `left` or `right`).
- `data-ch-theme`: `light` or `dark`, set by you on an ancestor.
- `data-ch-palette`: the palette, set by you on an ancestor.
- `data-ch-seq-tone`: the tone whose ramp a sequential scale uses.
- `data-ch-level`: the step (a number) of a mark in a stepped scale, for example a heatmap cell.
When there is no part for what you want to change, prefer a token. If neither exists, that is a gap in the public surface and worth an issue, not a reason to reach for a class.

Charts follow `prefers-color-scheme` until an ancestor sets `data-ch-theme="light"` or `data-ch-theme="dark"`; the attribute wins over the system setting, and a nested one wins over an outer one. That makes a dark panel on a light page a single attribute. Give the panel the theme's own `--ch-surface` and `--ch-ink` so the box matches the chart.
Next: [Palettes](/docs/palettes) swaps three of the tone colors, and [Dark mode](/docs/dark-mode) connects the theme to a toggle in your app.
